Author: B. Vijaysen Reddy
Bench: B. Vijaysen Reddy
 Honourable Sri Justice B. Vijaysen Reddy
 Writ Petition No.26729 Of 2025
Order :

(ORAL) This writ petition is filed by the petitioner seeking to declare the action of respondent No.4 in issuing the impugned rejection letter vide file No.011510/GHMC/5299/CHR2/2024-BP, dated 20.10.2024, rejecting his application for grant of building permission in respect of property bearing H.No.8-15-32/2/2, Plot No.833, admeasuring 462 square yards in Survey No.134/20, situated at Shashtripuram, Mailardevpally, Rajendranagar, Ranga Reddy, as being illegal, arbitrary and unconstitutional.

2. Heard Mr. Mohd. Abdul Hai, learned counsel for the petitioner; Mr. Raparthi Venkatesh, learned Standing Counsel for GHMC, appearing for respondents No.2 to 4; and perused the material on record.
3.
The petitioner claims to be the absolute owner and possessor of the subject property having purchased the same under registered sale deed bearing document No.1161 of 2019 dated 02.02.2019.
The petitioner initially submitted application dated 16.02.2022 with respondent No.3 for grant of building permission in respect of the subject property, however the same was lapsed.

Later, the petitioner submitted fresh application dated 19.10.2022 for grant of building permission in respect of building permission for construction of building comprising of stilt for parking + 3 upper floors in the subject property by paying requisite fees of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees ten thousand only).

As there was delay on the part of the respondent authorities in processing the building application, the petitioner filed W.P. No.5405 of 2025 before this Court which came up for hearing on 24.02.2025.
On that said date, the learned Standing Counsel for GHMC produced a copy of the impugned rejection letter dated 20.10.2024 and the said writ petition was dismissed as infructuous.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the impugned rejection letter dated 20.10.2024 is arbitrary and unsustainable.
The petitioner was given reasonable opportunity to submit relevant documents in respect of the subject property.
And that the subject property was not physically inspected, as such, the impugned rejection letter is in violation of principles of natural justice.

Learned counsel submitted that Market Value Certificate issued by the Sub-Registrar, Rajendra Nagar (Ex.P-2) dated 25.02.2025; a copy of sale deed bearing document No.1161 of 2019 dated 02.02.2019 (Ex.P-3), prima facie, show that the petitioner is the owner of the subject property.
Learned counsel relied on the judgment of this Court in W.P. No.358 of 2024 dated 08.01.2024 wherein it was held that the building permission cannot be refused only on the ground that it is Mohd. 1 likely to be affected in the proposed master plan.
5.

sentences.text: Learned Standing Counsel for GHMC submitted that apart from objection relating to the master plan, the petitioner is required to prove his title in respect of the subject property.

The Market Value Certificate (Ex.P-2) issued by the Sub-Registrar, Rajendra Nagar, shows that the subject property of the petitioner is covered by Court stay and included in the prohibitory list of properties.

6. This Court in W.P. No.358 of 2024 dated 08.01.2024 held as under:
"...
9.

This Court, in WP.No.29024 of 2023, dt.17.10.2023, took note of the dicta laid down by the erstwhile High Court of A.P. in G.Usha Rani vs State Of Andhra Pradesh,
wherein it has been held as under:
"It is incumbent on the part of the respondents to initiate proceedings under Section 18 of the AP Urban Areas (Development) Act, 1975 in accordance with the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 for acquisition of the land of the petitioner for road widening and pay compensation to the petitioner.

Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
If not, the petitioner would be deprived of her valuable property without compensation."
10.

This Court in WP.No.29024 of 2023 further observed that even if the master plan is notified, the authorities cannot seek to deny grant of permission, unless the property is being shown as open area in the master plan.

11. In the present case, since it is not shown to this Court of the respondents-authorities initiating any steps to acquire the land of the petitioner being shown as covered by Master Plan 100 feet road

,
the respondents-authorities cannot deprive the petitioner of enjoyment of her valuable property by making construction therein, by refusing to grant building permission. ..."

7. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner that reasonable opportunity of hearing was not given to the petitioner and that Ex.P-2 and P-3 have not been considered, which is in violation of principles of natural justice, this writ petition is disposed of directing respondent No.3 to consider the building application of the petitioner dated 19.10.2022 without reference to the objection with regard to the master plan in the impugned rejection letter dated 20.10.2022.

However, the petitioner is directed to comply with the other objections raised in the impugned rejection letter and also satisfy respondent No.3 with his title in respect of the subject property and that the subject property is not included in the prohibitory list of properties as shown in Ex.P-2.

As and when compliance is made by the petitioner, the building application shall be processed by giving opportunity of hearing to the petitioner and to all other concerned/interested persons and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, within a period of twenty one (21) days thereafter.
There shall be no order as to costs.
